card.title: Dark Matter, Black Holes and Gravitational Waves

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Dark matter** (~27% of the universe) supplies the unseen gravity that keeps galaxy rotation curves flat and bends light via lensing — it interacts gravitationally but not electromagnetically. **Dark energy** (~68%) is the uniform component making the expansion *accelerate* (1998 supernova surveys). Together the unseen is ~95% of everything.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - R_s = 2GM/c² - Dark matter ≈ 27%, dark energy ≈ 68%, ordinary matter ≈ 5% - Gravitational waves travel at c

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Dark matter clumps and pulls; dark energy spreads and pushes** — different beasts, both invisible.  ·  **A black hole's horizon for the Sun is only 3 km** — gravity compressed to a city's size.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Invisible 95% Everything we see — stars, gas, dust, us — is only ~5% of the universe. **Dark matter** holds galaxies together without shining; **dark energy** pushes the expansion faster; **black holes** trap light itself; and **gravitational waves** let us *hear* spacetime ring. Modern physics is mostly a search for the missing.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Dark matter Galaxy rotation curves refuse to fall off with distance as visible mass allows — the outer stars orbit as fast as the inner ones. An unseen mass component, **dark matter**, must supply the extra gravity: - ~5× more mass than ordinary (baryonic) matter — about 27% of the universe.…  ·  ### Deep dive: three windows on the invisible **Dark matter** betrays itself only by gravity: galaxy rotation curves stay flat far from the centre instead of falling as Kepler predicts, so each galaxy must carry several times more mass than its stars show. It neither emits nor absorbs light — hence *dark*.…
